messages:
mike: Heads-up — marketing briefed a feature flag ramp for next week, expected 2.8x peak QPS for ~36 hours. We need to confirm admit curve math so p95 stays <150ms and p99 <800ms. Can we run numbers for GPU-hour burn and soft-admit thresholds?

anya: thanks — do we have the baseline numbers? current p95/p99 and current qps?

mike: baseline peak QPS (last month) = 12k r/s. p95=120ms p99=650ms. Avg tokens per request ~45. GPU mix: 60% A100s, 40% H100s in prod regions.

oliver: note: APAC region has lower spare capacity (only 8 reserved GPUs right now). NA/EU have headroom. If ramp is global we’ll need to route/cap.

jess: cost side — 2.8x for 36h at current efficiency -> rough GPU-hour delta ~ (baseline_hours * 1.8). need exact.

anya: ok i’ll sketch the math quickly. assumptions: baseline peak sustained window = 6h, baseline QPS=12k. target peak = 2.8 * 12k = 33.6k. batching efficiency reduces tokens/GPU by factor 1.6 under ideal batching. estimated tokens/s per GPU (A100) = 2200 tokens/s (conservative). tokens/s per request = 45 * QPS.

anya: calculation: 
```
tokens_per_sec_target = 45 * 33600 = 1,512,000 tokens/s
effective_gpu_tokens = 2200 * 1.6 = 3520 tokens/s per GPU (after batching)
gpus_needed = ceil(tokens_per_sec_target / effective_gpu_tokens) = ceil(1,512,000 / 3520) = 430 GPUs
```

anya: current prod capacity (all regions) = 320 GPUs active. delta ~= 110 GPUs for peak window. For 36 hours, delta_gpu_hours = 110 * 36 = 3960 GPU-hours.

jess: rough cost estimate (on reserved mix): A100 equiv blended $2.3/hr -> 3960 * 2.3 = ~$9.1k additional spend (one-time for the event). we should budget ~12k to be safe (network, extra CPU, fallbacks).

oliver: admission control idea: soft-admit curve that starts shedding low-value requests when queue latency > p95 target. fallback to cheaper quantized variant (cpu/gpu mixed) for >90th percentile load.

mike: can you sketch the admit curve numbers? we want graceful degradation so p99 stays bounded.

anya: propose a two-stage admit policy: stage A = allow up to 350 GPUs equivalent (this preserves p95). stage B = soft-throttle to 0.7 of incoming QPS multilaterally (route 30% to cached responses / control plane tier) until autoscale finishes. if queue length > 2s then start stage B.

anya: config snippet (pseudo):
```
admit_policy:
  base_capacity_gpus: 320
  soft_threshold_queue_s: 0.5   # begin batching/fast-path tuning
  hard_threshold_queue_s: 2.0   # trigger soft-throttle
  throttle_fraction: 0.30
  fallback_variant: quantized-v2-cpu   # lower-cost, higher-latency model
  p95_target_ms: 150
  p99_target_ms: 800
```

oliver: region routing: enable cross-region spill (NA->EU) for stateless endpoints to use idle EU capacity, but respect data residency flags. APAC limited -> maybe prefer degraded responses for APAC unless we spin extra capacity there.

jess: agree on cross-region spill, but flag cost impact: additional egress ~1.4TB -> ~$250. include in the budget.

infra-costs: Budget estimation run finished: additional cost projection = $12,450 (gpu + egress + ops buffer). Marking for finance review. :white_check_mark:

mike: operational checklist before ramp:
- verify autoscaler policies will add 120 GPUs within 45 minutes (anya / eng-runtime)
- deploy admit_policy config to staging and run soak test (oliver)
- enable cross-region spill with opt-in flag for vendors (infra)
- create a runbook with rollback thresholds (p99 > 1200ms or error rate > 3%) (mike)

anya: i'll run an A/B simulation today using traffic replay. will post results here by EOD.

oliver: i'll reserve 120 spot-capacity units in NA and EU as buffer; if spot unavailable we'll convert to on-demand (cost impact noted).

mike: thanks team. If the simulation shows >15% variance in batching assumptions we reconvene and adjust throttle_fraction. :thumbsup:
